facets.title: 1. The WWHT template — What, Why, How, Test

facts.text: The order matters: reviewers read top-down and decide whether to keep reading after each section.

facets.title: 2. The two-tier reader pattern — skimmers above, nit-pickers below

facts.text: A PR has two audiences:
Skimmers - the manager, the on-call, the eventual archaeologist running git log six months from now.
Nit-pickers - the assigned reviewer.
Screenshot discipline:
Two screenshots side by side: Before and After.
Crop tight to the changed region.
For dark-mode features, include both light- and dark-mode screenshots.
Recording discipline:
Use recordings for interaction flows, animation, or anything that can't be captured in one frame.
Trim to ≤ 30 seconds.
Inline: The rationale for the design decision; the error message or log line; the before/after screenshots; a 3-line code snippet.
Link out: The full incident report; the original RFC; the customer ticket; the benchmark methodology; stack traces longer than 10 lines.
[Draft] or use GitHub's native "Draft PR" toggle
[Do not merge] - for PRs that exist for discussion only
[Stacked on #1234] - depends on another PR
When a feature can't reasonably fit in one reviewable PR (~400 lines is the soft ceiling):
PR #1: refactor / scaffolding - no behavior change.
PR #2: the substantive change - depends on #1.
PR #3: tests / docs / migration - depends on #2.
Mark each stacked PR's body with its position:

facets.title: 8. Checklists that get verified, not skipped

facts.text: [ ] Code follows best practices
[ ] npm run lint passes locally
[ ] npm run test passes locally
[ ] Manifest version bumped in manifest.json and package.json
[ ] Screenshot added for any UI change
Empty PR descriptions ("see commits")
Bullet list of every changed file - the diff already shows this
Screenshots without before/after
"Tested locally" with no steps
40-item checklist of every conceivable concern
Massive PRs (1,000+ lines) - split into a stack
Hiding the breaking-change disclosure - put BREAKING in the TL;DR
Graphite - Best practices for GitHub pull request descriptions
GitHub Docs - Creating a pull request template
Conventional Comments specification

facts.text: Draft the description in WWHT order (What, Why, How, Test), since reviewers read top-down and decide whether to keep reading after each section.

facts.text: Write for both audiences at once: a skimmable summary at the top for the manager or future archaeologist, and enough detail below for the assigned reviewer doing a line-by-line pass.

facts.text: Include tight before/after screenshots (both light- and dark-mode where relevant) or a trimmed recording for any visual or interaction change, rather than describing the change in prose alone.

facts.text: Split a change approaching the ~400-line soft ceiling into a stack (scaffolding, then substantive change, then tests/docs/migration), marking each PR's position and dependency explicitly in its body.

facts.text: The WWHT template and two-tier reader pattern assume reviewers actually read top-down; a reviewer who jumps straight to the diff may never see carefully structured context at the top of the description.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Stacked PRs reduce individual PR size but add coordination overhead — a reviewer needs to track dependency order across multiple PRs, which is more cognitively demanding than reviewing one large PR in isolation.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Long verification checklists tend to get rubber-stamped rather than actually checked once they exceed a handful of items, undermining the goal of checklists that get verified, not skipped.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: The line-count soft ceiling (~400 lines) is a heuristic, not a hard rule — some genuinely atomic changes, like a large generated-file update or a bulk rename, exceed it without being meaningfully splittable into a reviewable stack.
